title: Kanpur Logistics Park Pvt. Ltd. v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division, KESCO
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shashi Kant Gupta, J.; Manju Rani Chauhan, J.
disposition: Stay of recategorisation demand; arrears not insisted pending hearing.
headnote: On a writ challenging KESCO's 23.11.2018 recategorisation of the consumer from HV-2 to HV-1 and recovery of 2012 arrears first demanded in 2017, the Division Bench recorded that the matter required consideration, listed the petition after pleadings, and stayed the impugned order and insistence on arrears of Rs.34,74,876.59 (and interest) in the 16.12.2017 bill, subject to payment of current HV-2 dues.
facts: Kanpur Logistics Park Pvt. Ltd. challenged KESCO's 23.11.2018 order recategorising its Kanpur premises from HV-2 to HV-1 after a site visit and raising arrears from October 2012. It alleged no inspection report or notice, a still-subsisting HV-2 agreement, and a first demand only in September 2017, said to violate Section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 6.15 of the Supply Code, 2005. The 16.12.2017 bill claimed arrears of Rs.34,74,876.59.

holding_units.topic: interim stay of HV-1 recategorisation arrears
holding_units.holding: The challenge to KESCO's 23.11.2018 order recategorising the consumer from HV-2 to HV-1 and raising 2012 arrears requires consideration. Effect and operation of that order are stayed until further orders; the licensee shall not insist on deposit of arrears of Rs.34,74,876.59 in the bill dated 16.12.2017 or interest thereon, provided the petitioners continue to deposit current electricity dues at Tariff HV-2.

not_decided.point: Validity of HV-2 to HV-1 recategorisation without notice, inspection report, or cancellation of the HV-2 agreement
not_decided.note: Principal challenge; not decided on merits.

not_decided.point: Whether inclusion of 2012 arrears first demanded in September 2017 violates Section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 6.15 of the Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Argued; the Bench only recorded that the matter requires consideration.
